key_findings.statement: Pre-existing diseases are subject to a 48-month waiting period from the inception of the first policy. The insured has 27 months of continuous coverage, which is insufficient to satisfy the 48-month requirement.
The patient was admitted for 96 hours, satisfying the 24-hour minimum stay requirement for inpatient hospitalization.
Room rent is capped at 1% of the Sum Insured (5,000 INR), doctor fees at 25% (125,000 INR), and medical/diagnostic expenses at 40% (200,000 INR).
Pre and post-hospitalization expenses are only admissible if the primary inpatient claim is admissible.
The policy requires hospital registration or compliance with all minimum criteria; the supplied facts establish neither route.

citations.claim: Pre-existing diseases are subject to a 48-month waiting period from the inception of the first policy. The insured has 27 months of continuous coverage, which is insufficient to satisfy the 48-month requirement.
citations.quote:
1. Pre-existing diseases
Pre-existing diseases will not be covered until 48 months of continuous coverage have elapsed, since
inception of the first Policy with Us; but:
If You are presently covered and have been continuously covered without any break under:
i. An individual health insurance plan with an Indian insurer for the reimbursement of medical costs for
inpatient treatment in a Hospital,
OR
ii. Any other similar health insurance plan from Us, then, Pre-existing diseases exclusion of the Policy
stands deleted and shall be replaced entirely with the following:
i. The waiting period for all Pre-existing diseases shall be reduced by the number of Your continuous
preceding years of coverage under the previous health insurance Policy;
AND
ii. If the proposed Sum Insured for You is more than the Sum Insured applicable under the previous
health insurance Policy (other than as a result of the application of Cumulative Bonus), then the
reduced waiting period shall only apply to the extent of the Sum Insured under the previous health
insurance Policy.

semantic_checks.explanation: The policy mandates a 48-month waiting period for pre-existing diseases. With 27 months of continuous coverage, the requirement is not met.
The policy defines hospitalization as a minimum of 24 consecutive hours; the 96-hour admission exceeds this requirement.
The sub-limits are correctly calculated based on the 500,000 INR Sum Insured: 1% for room (5,000 INR), 25% for doctor fees (125,000 INR), and 40% for medicines/diagnostics (200,000 INR).
The policy definitions for pre- and post-hospitalization expenses explicitly state that admissibility is contingent upon the inpatient hospitalization claim being admissible.
The policy requires either registration under the Clinical Establishments Act or specific minimum criteria (nursing staff, bed count, etc.). The case facts do not provide evidence for either.
The calculation correctly applies the 1% sub-limit for room rent against the 500,000 INR Sum Insured.
The calculation correctly applies the 25% sub-limit for doctor fees against the 500,000 INR Sum Insured.
The calculation correctly applies the 40% sub-limit for medicines and diagnostics against the 500,000 INR Sum Insured.
